title: Type 1 Diabetes in Adults: Annual Review and Sick-Day Rules

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult type 1 diabetes annual review, hypoglycaemia awareness, complication surveillance and documented sick-day plan using NICE NG17.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi-specific annual-review intervals and sick-day insulin algorithms were not opened.
Individual insulin correction doses and ketone thresholds must come from the diabetes team's written plan.

pathophysiology.summary: Autoimmune beta-cell loss causes absolute insulin deficiency. Insulin omission during illness can accelerate ketogenesis and diabetic ketoacidosis. Excess insulin relative to carbohydrate or activity causes hypoglycaemia. Chronic glycaemic exposure drives microvascular and macrovascular complications.
keyMechanisms: Autoimmune beta-cell loss causes absolute insulin deficiency.
Insulin omission during illness can accelerate ketogenesis and diabetic ketoacidosis.
Excess insulin relative to carbohydrate or activity causes hypoglycaemia.
Chronic glycaemic exposure drives microvascular and macrovascular complications.

symptoms: Hypoglycaemia, hyperglycaemia, recurrent illness-related ketones, visual change, neuropathic symptoms or reduced wellbeing.
physicalSigns: Injection-site lipohypertrophy, BP abnormality, foot-risk findings or complication signs.
redFlags: Vomiting with ketones, inability to retain fluids, rapid breathing, drowsiness, severe hypoglycaemia, pregnancy or acute foot/visual symptoms.
precipitants: Intercurrent illness, missed insulin, pump interruption, incorrect injection technique, steroid exposure, alcohol and major changes in food or activity.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Atypical course or preserved endogenous insulin may prompt specialist reassessment; do not stop insulin while clarifying.

clinicalManagement.title: Annual structured review
actions: Agree priorities and review HbA1c/glucose data, hypoglycaemia awareness, insulin delivery, injection sites, education, mental health, driving, pregnancy planning and complications.
Measure TSH and ensure eye, kidney, foot and cardiovascular-risk surveillance is current.

clinicalManagement.title: Rehearse the sick-day plan
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At annual review and after every illness-related event
actions: Confirm the person has written instructions for glucose and ketone monitoring, fluids, carbohydrate and insulin adjustment from the diabetes team.
Do not stop basal insulin; use only the person's documented correction plan.

clinicalManagement.title: Urgent illness escalation
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Same day or emergency according to the written plan
actions: Escalate vomiting, inability to retain fluids, rising ketones, rapid breathing, drowsiness or severe hypoglycaemia.
Check pump delivery promptly when glucose or ketones rise unexpectedly.

medicationPlan.note: Continue individual basal-bolus or pump therapy. Sick-day correction doses are patient-specific and must come from the diabetes team's written protocol; this topic does not invent them.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: At least annually, with priorities agreed with the adult.

teaching.scope: Adult type 1 diabetes annual review, hypoglycaemia awareness, complication surveillance and documented sick-day plan using NICE NG17.
learningObjectives: Use a written sick-day plan without stopping basal insulin.
pitfalls: Giving a generic correction dose without the person's plan.
Treating HbA1c in isolation from hypoglycaemia and quality of life.
keyPoints: Ketone monitoring forms part of sick-day self-management.

references.title: NICE NG17: Type 1 diabetes in adults

patientEducation: Provide updated diabetes-team and out-of-hours contact details and confirm teach-back of sick-day rules.
lifestyleAndDiet: Support carbohydrate counting, safe exercise, alcohol safety, oral health and smoking cessation.
mdtReferrals: Adult diabetes team, diabetes educator, dietitian, podiatry, retinal screening, renal and pregnancy services as indicated.
dischargeCriteria: Annual plan updated, complications surveillance arranged, sick-day plan available and urgent escalation advice understood.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: At least annually, with earlier review after severe hypoglycaemia, DKA, pregnancy planning, recurrent ketones or major treatment change.
